answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to stake a small, verifiable work history before it earns trust — not just a wallet address. Think of reputation as basalt: layered slowly over time, hard to fake at scale. A newcomer starts in a low-trust haven, limited to tiny trades, and only gains wider access as its ferrous record of completed, honest work accumulates. Forging thousands of identities becomes uneconomical because each one must pay the same slow cost.
